sections.section_name: Section A - Choose the Correct Answer

questions.question_text: What is the primary source of fresh water on the Earth that fills up rivers and lakes?
Where does a natural river usually begin its journey before flowing down to the plains?
options: A) High up in the mountains
C) In the middle of a desert
D) From a city water tank
questions.answer: A) High up in the mountains

questions.question_text: Which of the following physical features acts as a natural boundary to the north of India?
How can students actively make their school a happy and safe place for everyone?
options: A) By fighting over playground swings
B) By sharing and caring for each other
questions.answer: B) By sharing and caring for each other

questions.question_text: Early humans transitioned from hunting and gathering to which activity to get a steady supply of food?
What do geographers call the specific place where a river finally meets the sea or ocean?
Which traditional method helps in collecting and saving rainwater for future use?
India is uniquely famous around the world as a land of 'Unity in _____'.
Which of the following is considered a major staple food crop grown in the southern and eastern parts of India?
Which important social value helps students solve conflicts peacefully in a school environment?
List two simple ways you can save water at home every day to prevent its wastage. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: I can save water by turning off the tap while brushing my teeth and fixing any leaking pipes immediately to stop unnecessary water wastage.

questions.question_text: What happens to the speed and shape of a river when it leaves the mountains and reaches the flat plains? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: When a river reaches the flat plains, its speed decreases significantly. It becomes much wider, flows calmly, and begins to deposit fertile soil along its banks.

questions.question_text: Why is the discovery of farming considered an important milestone in early human history? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Farming allowed early humans to settle in one permanent place instead of wandering. It provided a steady food supply, leading to the growth of villages.

questions.question_text: Mention two responsibilities of a student to keep their school environment clean and welcoming. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A student should always throw garbage in the provided dustbins and avoid scribbling on the classroom walls or desks to maintain a clean learning environment.

questions.question_text: Why is India commonly referred to as a country of rich and diverse cultures? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: India has diverse cultures because people across different regions speak various languages, celebrate different festivals, wear unique traditional clothes, and eat distinct types of food.

questions.question_text: Imagine you are a small paper boat sailing down a river from the mountains to the sea. Describe your journey and what you see. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: My journey starts as a bumpy ride through narrow, fast-flowing mountain streams. As I enter the plains, the water becomes calm and wide, passing green agricultural fields and bustling villages, until I finally float gently into the vast, salty ocean.

questions.question_text: Imagine you are traveling across India on a train from the north to the south. Describe the changes you would see in the physical landscape. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Looking out the window, I would first see the snowy peaks of the Himalayas, then travel through the flat, fertile northern plains. Later, I would cross dry plateaus before finally reaching the humid, lush green coastal areas near the sea.

questions.question_text: Explain how you would organize an awareness campaign in your school to teach younger students about the importance of saving water. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: I would organize a special morning assembly featuring a short, fun play showing the severe effects of water scarcity. We would display colorful posters with catchy slogans like 'Save Water, Save Life' around the school corridors. Finally, we would ask students to pledge to close running taps immediately.

questions.question_text: Describe how the journey of food from a farm to our plates shows the hard work of many people, and explain why we should never waste it. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Farmers work tirelessly for months in the sun to sow, grow, and harvest crops. Then, workers transport the food to markets, and shopkeepers sell it to our parents, who cook it for us. Because so much human effort goes into this entire journey, we must respect food by never wasting a single bite.
